s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hepatic masses with abnormal liver function tests and characteristic imaging findings
salient_findings: Multiple well-defined hypoechoic hepatic masses on ultrasonography
Mildly elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT)
Characteristic imaging features on CT, MRI, and PET
key_facts: 48-year-old man with no prior medical history
Three hepatic masses in segments 1, 6, and 2
Mass sizes: 67×53 mm, 13 mm, and 9 mm
Normal total bilirubin (0.6 mg/dL) and albumin (4.2 g/dL)
Mildly elevated AST (37 IU/L), ALT (70 IU/L), ALP (176 U/L), and GGT (170 IU/L)
Normal tumor markers (alpha-fetoprotein, PIVKA-II, CA19-9)
Dynamic contrast-enhanced CT showed peripheral early ring enhancement and heterogeneous internal enhancement
EOB-MRI revealed hypointense mass on T1-weighted images and hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images
FDG-PET showed no radiotracer accumulation in hepatic lesions
Hepatic arteriography demonstrated hypervascular masses without pooling
Gastroscopy and colonoscopy were unremarkable

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor with characteristic imaging findings and abnormal liver function tests

shortlist.label: Hepatic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor with potential for malignancy and similar imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor with characteristic imaging findings and potential for growth

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign liver tumor with characteristic imaging findings

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor with abnormal liver function tests and characteristic imaging findings

raw.rationale: The patient has multiple hepatic masses with heterogeneous internal enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced CT and hypervascular masses on hepatic arteriography, which are characteristic features of hepatocellular carcinoma. Although tumor markers are within normal limits, the imaging findings and mildly elevated liver enzymes support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatic adenoma
rejected.why: Hepatic adenomas typically have a more homogeneous appearance on imaging and are less likely to have multiple lesions.

rejected.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia
rejected.why: Focal nodular hyperplasia typically has a central scar and a more homogeneous appearance on imaging, which is not consistent with the patient's findings.

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: Hemangiomas typically have a characteristic appearance on imaging with peripheral nodular enhancement and centripetal filling, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma typically has a more aggressive appearance on imaging with irregular margins and heterogeneous enhancement, but the patient's tumor markers and imaging findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.
